The derivation holds. The sum has 10 terms, and the product-to-sum identity gives $2S = 10\cos(\pi/6) - \sum_{j=1}^{10}\cos\left(\frac{(2j+1)\pi}{12}\right)$. The cosine sum runs over odd multiples of $\pi/12$ from $3\pi/12$ to $21\pi/12$; the values cancel in pairs, leaving $-2\cos(\pi/12)$. So $S = \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2} + \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)$, and $\cos(\pi/12) = \frac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}}}{2}$ is correct. A direct numerical sum of the ten products also gives about 5.29606, matching 5.296053 within rounding.
